definitions.explanation: Clothes and merchandise meant for the hot months — light fabrics, short sleeves, sandals. Mainly a retail and wardrobe word, used when shops change their stock over and when households swap seasonal clothes.

examples.japanese: そろそろ{夏物|なつもの}を{出|だ}そう。
examples.english: It's about time to get the summer clothes out.

examples.japanese: デパートで{夏物|なつもの}のセールが{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The summer clothing sale has started at the department store.

examples.japanese: {衣替|ころもが}えをして、{冬物|ふゆもの}をしまい、{夏物|なつもの}を{取|と}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: I changed over my wardrobe, putting away the winter things and taking out the summer ones.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {夏物|なつもの}を{出|だ}す/しまう: to get out / put away summer clothes
- {夏物|なつもの}セール: summer clothing sale
- {夏物|なつもの}{衣料|いりょう}: summer apparel

SEASONAL SERIES:
The same {物|もの} pattern names each season's goods:
- {春物|はるもの}: spring wear
- {秋物|あきもの}: autumn wear
- {冬物|ふゆもの}: winter wear

RELATED WORDS:
- {衣替|ころもが}え: the seasonal changeover of clothing, done around June 1 and October 1
